crime.over80: More than 80 km/h over the limit is a criminal offense (fine up to KRW 300,000 or detention), not a traffic fine. Points: {pts} (Road Traffic Act Art. 154).
crime.over100: More than 100 km/h over means a fine up to KRW 1,000,000 or detention, and for a third offense up to 1 year in prison or KRW 5,000,000. Points: {pts} (Road Traffic Act Arts. 151-2, 153).

result.zoneOn: Higher {zone} rates (8 am to 8 pm) applied.
result.zoneOff: Even in a {zone}, regular rates apply outside 8 am to 8 pm.
result.zoneNa: This violation has no protected-zone surcharge, so regular rates apply.
result.zoneCrosswalk: The camera penalty for crosswalk violations in protected zones uses regular rates.
result.noCut: This penalty is not eligible for the early-payment discount (Enforcement Rule Annex 39).
result.twoHourOn: KRW 10,000 added for parking 2 hours or more in the same spot.
result.beltPassenger: If a passenger is unbelted, the driver also gets a KRW 30,000 penalty (KRW 60,000 if the passenger is under 13).
result.intersectionNote: Entering a jammed intersection past the stop line and blocking traffic is charged the same.
result.convert: If you identify the driver when responding to a penalty notice, a fine and points replace the penalty (Road Traffic Act Art. 160(4)).
result.disclaimer: Reference amounts calculated from the Road Traffic Act enforcement decree and rules. The actual notice prevails, and accidents, drunk or unlicensed driving change the penalty.

plan.title: Fine amount by payment deadline
plan.note: If unpaid after the 20 days, a summary trial is requested. Paying 50% extra before the request or ruling ends it. Not attending the summary trial within 60 days after the deadline adds 40 points.

points.title: Suspension or revocation by accumulated points
points.label: Current points
points.hint: Enter your points from the police traffic portal (eFine). Points are added only for police-stop fines.
points.suspend: License suspension. At 1 day per point, that is {days} days.
points.revoke: {y1}+ points within a year: license revocation.
points.rules: {at}+ points means suspension (1 point = 1 day); {y1} in 1 year, {y2} in 2 years or {y3} in 3 years means revocation (Enforcement Rule Annex 28). Your input is treated as the last year's total.

guide.title: Penalties, fines and points in a nutshell

diff.title: Penalty vs fine
items: A penalty (gwataeryo) goes to the vehicle owner when the driver is not identified, e.g. by a speed camera. No points.
A fine (beomchikgeum) is issued when police identify the driver on the spot. Points come with it.
For the same violation the penalty is equal to or higher than the fine, but carries no points.
If you identify the driver after a penalty notice, it becomes a fine with points.

pay.title: Paying and appealing
items: Check, pay and respond on the police portal Gyotong Minwon 24 (eFine, efine.go.kr). Parking penalties are mostly issued by city or district offices, so check the payee on the notice.
Paying a penalty before the comment deadline gives 20% off only for violations listed in Enforcement Rule Annex 39, such as parking, speeding up to 20 km/h and unbelted passengers.
To dispute a penalty, file a written objection within 60 days of the notice. The penalty then loses effect and goes to court (Act on the Regulation of Violations of Public Order Art. 20).
Unpaid penalties get a 3% surcharge, then 1.2% per month for up to 60 months (same Act Art. 24).
Pay fines within 10 days, or within the next 20 days with 20% added. After that the case goes to summary trial (Road Traffic Act Arts. 164, 165).

points.title: Managing and reducing points
items: Points accumulate over the 3 years before a violation. 40+ points means suspension (1 day per point); 121 in 1 year, 201 in 2 or 271 in 3 means revocation.
Below 40 points, they expire after 1 year without violations or accidents since the last one.
Below 40 points, completing the recommended special traffic safety course (point reduction) removes 20 points.
If suspended, the law-compliance course cuts 20 days, and the field participation course cuts 30 more.
A no-violation pledge kept for 1 year earns 10 bonus points that offset a future suspension (National Police Agency notice).

zone.title: School, senior and disabled zones
items: Between 8 am and 8 pm, penalties for signal, speeding and parking violations in protected zones are higher (Decree Annex 7).
Fines are higher for signal, speeding, crosswalk, no-entry and parking violations (Decree Annex 10).
Points double for speeding over 20 km/h, signal violations and failing to protect pedestrians; over 80 km/h is 120 points. In school zones, even up to 20 km/h over is 15 points (Rule Annex 28).
Outside 8 am to 8 pm, regular rates apply.

items.q: How much is a speeding penalty or fine?
items.a: For a car: up to 20 km/h over is a KRW 40,000 penalty or KRW 30,000 fine; 20–40 over is 70,000 / 60,000 (15 points); 40–60 over is 100,000 / 90,000 (30 points); over 60 is 130,000 / 120,000 (60 points). More than 80 km/h over is a criminal offense, not a fine.

items.q: How much is a school zone penalty?
items.a: Between 8 am and 8 pm, for a car: KRW 130,000 for a signal violation, 70,000 for up to 20 km/h over, 100,000 for 20–40 over and 120,000 for parking (130,000 after 2 hours). Police-stop fines are higher too and points double for signal and speeding.

items.q: Do I get points if I pay a penalty?
items.a: No. A penalty is a charge on the vehicle owner and carries no points. If you identify the driver and switch to a fine, points apply.

items.q: Is the 20% early-payment discount available for every penalty?
items.a: No. Only violations listed in Enforcement Rule Annex 39 (parking, speeding up to 20 km/h, unbelted passengers, etc.) get 20% off when paid before the comment deadline. Signal violations and speeding over 20 km/h get no discount.

items.q: How many points lead to a suspension?
items.a: 40 or more points means suspension, counted as 1 day per point. 121 points in 1 year, 201 in 2 or 271 in 3 means revocation.
Below 40 points, they expire after 1 year without violations or accidents since the last one. The point-reduction course can also remove 20 points.

items.q: What if I pay a fine late?
items.a: If not paid within 10 days, pay 20% more within the next 20 days. After that a summary trial is requested, which is cancelled if you pay 50% extra before the ruling.

guide.disclaimer: A reference calculation based on the statutes, not legal advice. Follow the notice and the enforcing agency for the actual penalty.
